audits.mathematicalReason: Let x index the front-view columns, y the side-view columns, and z the levels, starting at 0. The upper cube must occupy (0,1,1). At least three cubes are needed to produce the three squares in either projection. With exactly three, the two lower cubes must cover both x-values and both y-values. Their positions are therefore either {(0,0,0),(1,1,0)} or {(0,1,0),(1,0,0)}. In the first case the upper cube has no face-sharing neighbor; in the second case (1,0,0) has none. Four cubes suffice at (0,1,1), (0,1,0), (0,0,0), and (1,1,0). This proves a universal lower bound and supplies an attaining construction, matching the extremal scope without assuming a stronger connectivity condition.

audits.mathematicalReason: Write e = AE and let T be the tangency point on CE. Equal tangents give ET = EA = e and CT = CB = 2, so CE = e + 2. The right triangle CDE gives (e + 2)² = 4 + (2 − e)², hence e = 1/2 and CE = 5/2. The coordinate route is also valid: take A=(0,0), C=(2,2), and circle center O=(1,0). For CE written y−2=m(x−2), perpendicular distance from O to the tangent is 1, giving |2−m|/sqrt(1+m²)=1 and m=3/4. Its tangency point is (2/5,4/5), on the upper semicircle and within CE. Thus cnm_262 is directly exercised by the perpendicular-distance route; equal tangent lengths provide a valid alternative, not an additional universally required method.

Each join removes two unit faces from the exterior, so the surface area is 36 − 2·5 = 26 square inches, including all exterior faces whether visible or hidden in the drawing. audits.mathematicalReason: Internal tangency and the opposite diameter endpoints imply that the two large-circle centers are A and B, separated by 2. If P and Q are their intersection points, triangle ABP is equilateral with side 2, and each sector forming the common lens has central angle 120°. The midpoint of AB is also the midpoint of PQ; the half-chord length is sqrt(2²−1²)=√3. Each triangle APQ or BPQ therefore has area √3. The lens area is 2(4π/3−√3)=8π/3−2√3. The entire radius-1 disk lies in this lens, so removing its area π gives 5π/3−2√3. The proposed sector, composite-area, tangency, triangle, and circle scopes all support this derivation.

audits.mathematicalReason: The four vacant seats form a uniformly distributed four-element subset of the twelve seats, giving C(12,4)=495 outcomes. With no adjacent vacancies, a row can have no vacancy, one vacancy in any of three positions, or two vacancies only at its two ends. The possible row-vacancy counts are (1,1,1,1), (2,1,1,0), and (2,2,0,0), contributing 3⁴=81, 4·3·3²=108, and C(4,2)=6 outcomes. The complement therefore has 195 outcomes, so the required probability is (495−195)/495=20/33. Direct favorable counting is also valid: patterns (3,1,0,0), (2,2,0,0), and (2,1,1,0) contribute 36, 48, and 216 respectively. This supports both optional routes without treating rows as independent probability events.
